title: Career roadmap · Professor
summary: Build an academic career in science, technology and innovation policy through rigorous policy research, quantitative analysis, institutional studies, teaching, publications, grants and engagement with government and research organizations.

facts.Timeline assumption: The roadmap assumes a 2026-start Ph.D. research pathway. Early years focus on policy-methods depth and a distinctive research question; later years emphasize independent scholarship, grant funding, teaching, doctoral supervision, policy engagement and academic leadership.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Establish expertise in innovation studies, science policy, economics, governance, research methods and evidence-based policy analysis.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Build an independent research niche such as R&D policy, innovation economics, research governance, technology regulation or emerging-technology policy.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead a research group or centre, supervise doctoral researchers, secure interdisciplinary grants and advise policy institutions.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Shape national and international STI research agendas, lead academic centres and connect evidence with technology and innovation policy decisions.

rows.text: Science-policy foundations, innovation theory and research design

Map a national research ecosystem and identify measurable policy interventions
Complete a technology-policy assessment covering benefits, risks and implementation options
Produce a technology-transfer/IP policy analysis with evidence and recommendations
Prepare a complete interdisciplinary research proposal with objectives, methods and milestones
Produce a policy brief translating a research finding into actionable recommendations
Maintain a research portfolio with publications, policy outputs, collaborations and a defined research agenda

blocks.text: Ph.D. routes

The long-term academic role should combine scholarly authority with policy relevance. Build a research centre or program that can evaluate R&D investment, innovation performance, technology risks, research institutions and emerging technologies using credible evidence. Develop long-term relationships with universities, government departments, research agencies, industry and international policy organizations while retaining methodological independence.
